pr_title: Fixes for ublox SARA modem driver
pr_body:
This PR is a combination of fixes for a wide variety of issues noticed on the SARA-R4 modem:
- MQTT wasn't working correctly
- http_get sample was crashing
- echo_client wasn't working
- odd behavior was happening in LwM2M client under load

Some additional authors contributed patches which were added here for easy testing due to the # of changes:
@weinholtendian and @hwilmers

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/21764
Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/21328
pr_comments:
These fixes are related to: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/21764  But don't quite fix all issues.  MQTT is still having problems due to the way it uses recv() with perfectly sized buffers to parse the socket data.

The SARA-R4 modem AT commands may have a bug where the full packet data needs to be queried at a time.
@gpaquet85 @weinholtendian @WilliamGFish FYI
NOTE: More work coming on this PR.

> > MQTT is still having problems due to the way it uses recv() with perfectly sized buffers to parse the socket data.
> 
> @mike-scott What kind of problems are there in MQTT, can you elaborate more?
> cc: @rlubos

@jukkar @rlubos 
Yes, sorry to be a bit vague.  I was trying to make better use of the modem's data buffer by only pulling data as it was needed via the recv() call (based on the length of the buffer passed in).

The MQTT library parses individual packets bytes at a time, so this leads to successive calls to the modem to retrieve data for the same packet.  The way this modem driver works is it keeps track of how much data in in the modem's buffer (split up by packet). My handling of the packet sizes didn't allow for partial retrieval of packets in this way.

I need to think about how to handle this.

I tested this PR with Sara R410, with following results:
- MQTT client works fine
- echo_client (TCP) works fine with small chunks (up to 1023 bytes)
- echo_client (TCP) fails with chunks >= 1024 bytes

I then discovered that in case of these failures, the +USOWR fails with an error message from the modem ("ERROR"), immediately followed by a +UUSORD message from the modem.

To me it looks like a solution could be to let the application poll for incoming data in between multiple calls to send(). So should this be solved in the driver, or rather in the application?
Apropos TLS: Is there a way to use this driver with TLS, other than offloading it? Are there any hooks one can use to use mbedTLS?

Thanks for testing, let me take a look at the >= 1024 use case to see where the fix would best be located.  In a perfect world, we fix that in the driver so that samples don't need to be changed.  However, there is some "bad behavior" in the samples sometimes which can be changed.

> The main reason for me _not_ wanting to offload SSL in the esp8266, or any external device really, is that data will be passed in clear text over the UART.

When I looked at how the SSL certificates would be setup for ESP8266, it seems like they needed to be written to flash to avoid this situation.

`AT+CIPSSLCCONF=2` means (taken from AT command doc):
```
bit1:if set to be 1, CA will be enabled, so ESP8266 can verify SSL server; if 0, then will not.
```

And the example AT command uses are:
```
AT+CIPSNTPCFG=1,8 // set SNTP timezone
AT+CIPSNTPTIME? // get SNTP time
AT+CIPSSLCCONF=2
AT+CIPSTART="SSL","192.168.3.38",8443
```

There doesn't seem to be a time when cleartext SSL information would be used over UART.

> There doesn't seem to be a time when cleartext SSL information would be used over UART.

Right but then when you send or read data over that connection the data will be sent unencrypted over the UART? Maybe I'm missing something 🤔

> Right but then when you send or read data over that connection the data will be sent unencrypted over the UART? Maybe I'm missing something

Yes, this would be true.  UART lines are a fairly easy physical attack vector.
Unfortunately, this isn't limited to SSL connections.  The Wifi AP password is sent in clear text, etc.

Rebased on today's master with the last set of changes:
- Remove hex mode.  It limits the send/receive MTU on SARA-R4 to 512 which is too restrictive.  We can now handle this inside the modem commands by returning EAGAIN if the command doesn't have enough data to finish parsing.
- parse_params() shouldn't parse as many delimiters as it can, instead it should honor the arg_count value and stop once it receives that # of params
- And a few minor changes

I've a question, pardon my ignorance if I'm overlooking something here.

I've implemented this driver and have it working for the most part. When I open a socket and send data to an echo server, I get back a response which shows as an unsolicited message with a 'number bytes ready' count. When I use the recv() function to read incoming data, I'm unable to get data that arrived before I called the recv() function but has already been handled with the modem_socket_data_ready() function. It looks like, while in modem_socket_wait_data() it only waits for fresh data to come in and doesn't detect recently buffered data.

Is this the proper functionality of recv() or am I doing something wrong?

> Is this the proper functionality of recv() or am I doing something wrong?

@Brietoe TCP data should never disappear merely because recv() was called too late. The driver is in control of when it reads from the modem's socket buffer, and it does not need to read if it doesn't have anywhere to save the data. Sounds to me like a pretty severe bug if data disappears this way. UDP is a slightly different story.

@weinholtendian Okay, that's what I thought. I don't want to jump to conclusions and claim that the offload_recv() does indeed suffer from this issue because I had to make some modifications to the code to fit my use case. The data is still accessible through workarounds but I'm just not able to retrieve it using recv().

I'd love to know if anyone else is also experiencing this issue.

issue_context.title: Apparent network context leak with offloading driver (u-blox Sara r4)
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
I have an issue when I try to make multiple MQTT connection/disconnection.
I focused on net_context management.
Indeed in net_context_get function, I saw that I reached CONFIG_NET_MAX_CONTEXTS (equal to 10 in my prj.conf).
For your information, I use UBLOX sara r4 driver (on zephyr 1.14.1) and I wonder if contexts are well managed in this revision (or new one?), especially when socket is closed ?


**To Reproduce**
Compiling https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/master/samples/net/mqtt_publisher:
1. mkdir build; cd build
2. cmake -DBOARD=boards\nrf52840_pca10059 -DSHIELD=sparkfun_sara_r4 -DCONF_FILE="prj.conf overlay-wncm14a2a.conf" (I am not sure of this configuration because I did this with our own board)
3. make
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
After 10 (equal to CONFIG_NET_MAX_CONTEXTS) connection/disconnection in TCP, you should have this behavior: 
[try_to_connect:233] mqtt_connect: -2 <ERROR>.

**Impact**
It is not possible to communicate anymore in MQTT (TCP) because it is not possible to connect to broker after CONFIG_NET_MAX_CONTEXTS attemps

**Screenshots or console output**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33019844/70696083-4466a700-1cc3-11ea-846d-59d49953f279.png)


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain ARM-GCC
 - Tag: v1.14.1


**Additional context**
I also saw an issue in UBLOX SARA R4 socket close management when URC +UUCLOSE happens.
I am not sure that this issue is linked to our issue. Moreover, maybe it is well managed in new revision
